questions.q: What does Git actually track when a dataset is versioned with DVC?
options: The full dataset, compressed
A screenshot of the data
Only the folder name of the dataset
A small .dvc pointer file containing the data's content hash and size
questions.explain: DVC stores the data in its cache and remote; Git tracks only the tiny pointer file, whose hash changes when the data changes.

questions.q: You append 200 rows to a DVC-tracked CSV. Which command shows that the data no longer matches its pointer?
options: git status, because Git tracks the CSV
dvc status
dvc init
pip freeze
questions.explain: The CSV is ignored by Git, so git status stays quiet. dvc status compares the file's hash with the pointer and reports it as modified.

questions.q: What did dvc add refuse to do in the lesson, and why?
options: It refused to hash files over 10 MB
It refused because there was no remote configured
It refused because the CSV was already tracked by Git, and a file can have only one owner
It refused because the file had a header row
questions.explain: DVC reported that the output was already tracked by SCM. Remove the file from Git with git rm --cached first, then add it to DVC.

questions.q: How do you restore the dataset used at an older commit?
options: Check out that commit's .dvc pointer file with Git, then run dvc checkout
Run dvc init again
Re-download it from the internet
Edit the md5 value by hand and hope
questions.explain: The pointer from the old commit names the old content; dvc checkout copies the matching data from the cache (or dvc pull fetches it from the remote).

questions.q: Why is a DVC remote needed in a team, given that the cache already holds every version?
options: The cache is only on one person's machine; a remote gives everyone shared storage to push to and pull from
Remotes make the hash shorter
Git refuses to work without a remote
Remotes are only for models, not data
questions.explain: The local cache is not shared. dvc push uploads data to the remote and dvc pull downloads it, for example on a new machine or CI runner.
